text.p: Mozambique is to toughen environmental protection after new legislation passed its last significant hurdle in parliament.

Following Tuesday's passage, a final vote will be taken on the framework bill on conservation later this month, but this is a formality. President Joaquim Chissano will be free to promulgate the law in August.
The bill passed its second reading with no substantial objections from opposition parties.
It will make life more difficult for polluters, outlawing any practice that causes deforestation, erosion or any other environmental damage "beyond the legally established limits".

All activities threatening the survival of endangered species or otherwise damaging the poor southern African country's biodiversity are forbidden, and the government is charged with restoring damaged wildlife habitats.

No houses or other structures may be built where they cause "a significant negative impact on the environment", particularly along the coast, in wetlands, in places threatened with erosion, and other ecologically sensitive areas.

Mozambique, devastated by 16 years of war until 1992 and now showing some success in rebuilding its economy, is courting foreign investors including developers keen to build tourist resorts in pristine coastal regions.
